_README: Additional / curated sanctions lists loaded ONLY by scripts/sanctions-screen.mjs (not by the watcher's strict loader). A source may be remote (`url` + `parser`) or in-repo curated (`file`, parser 'curated'). Set `enabled:false` to keep a source configured but skipped. A remote source that fails or parses 0 names, or a curated list with no entries, degrades coverage (reported loudly) — never a silent all-clear.

sources.name: Argentina — RePET Entidades (terror-linked entities)
sources._note: RePET entidades — terror-linked ENTITIES sibling of the loaded personas.json (same /xml/ dir, keyless JSON). ENABLED 2026-08-05 on source-probe evidence (run 31030989375): the runner fetched real JSON (http 200, 156KB). The feed is the UN-consolidated-list schema in JSON (FIRST_NAME holds the entity name; ENTITY_ALIAS[].ALIAS_NAME the a.k.a. names) — hence parser 'unjson' (concatenates the ordered UN name parts and captures ALIAS_NAME), NOT the generic 'json' walker which read only FIRST_NAME and dropped the aliases.

sources.name: CIS / Caucasus gated cluster: Kyrgyzstan / Moldova / Armenia
sources._note:
2026-08-05 survey record: Kazakhstan's Web-SFM endpoint became key-gated ~Sep 2025 (rejected under the keyless doctrine); Kyrgyzstan's FIU XML rotates its filename each update and Azerbaijan's FMS XML sits behind an index page — both need HTML link-discovery the single-GET fetcher deliberately does not do (a future fetch feature, not a source entry); Georgia's Otkhozoria-Tatunashvili list (~33 names) and Armenia's national designations publish as gazette HTML / dated PDFs (curated path); Moldova's CAS-SIS list consolidates UN lists already screened. One documented stub, enabled:false — survey record, never counted as coverage. VERIFIED 2026-09-25: Kazakhstan confirmed still uncovered by OpenSanctions (their own country page: 'we are not yet including any programs targeting entities in Kazakhstan'). Moldova's CAS-SIS assumption checked directly against OpenSanctions' md_terror_sanctions (709 entities, fetched live) - its own first record cites a UN Security Council 1718 Committee (DPRK) designation, consistent with this being substantially UN-derived; kept disabled, this appears correct rather than corrected. Georgia and Armenia: no OpenSanctions mirror found today either. Georgia (Otkhozoria-Tatunashvili List) split out 2026-09-26 - see ge-ot-list above. Also confirmed today, more concretely than before: OpenSanctions' own kz_afmrk_sanctions dataset page states in its own words that Kazakhstan's list 'is no longer accessible from the official source, an API key is now required... correspondence with the Financial Monitoring Agency for broader access has not been successful' - i.e. even OpenSanctions, with more standing than this project, could not get it either. Armenia: OpenSanctions tracks only parliamentary-membership data for Armenia, no sanctions list.

ATTEMPTED HAND-CURATION 2026-09-26: confirmed Kyrgyzstan's list is maintained by the State Financial Intelligence Service (fiu.gov.kg / SFIS), under the 2006 AML/CFT law - their own site confirms the agency and legal basis but its list page uses the rotating-filename pattern this file already flagged, and it isn't surfaced by search (an indexed rotating file rarely is). Azerbaijan: the discovered hms.gov.az XML link from the 2026-08-05 survey was re-checked and still resolves, but its dateGenerated is still 2023-12-27 with no newer version found - unchanged from before, still not enabled pending someone confirming whether that source republishes at all. No progress on Armenia this session beyond the OpenSanctions catalog check already recorded above.

FINAL VERDICT 2026-09-26 on Armenia: found only historical (2002-era) UN counter-terrorism cooperation reporting, no evidence of an active distinct national designation list today. Treating this the same as Ghana and Korea: not a file I failed to find, but a country whose own regime produces nothing beyond the UN-consolidated source already screened here.

DEFINITIVE FINDING 2026-09-26 on Kyrgyzstan (supersedes the earlier 'rotating filename, unindexed' note - the real reason is stronger than that): the FIU's own homepage (fiu.gov.kg) states outright, for its most recent 2026 orders (22.04.2026 and 29.04.2026, so the underlying list is genuinely active, not defunct), that the updated content is 'находящиеся в закрытой части сайта ГСФР' - located in the CLOSED part of the FIU's site. This isn't a discovery problem a browser would fix; the Kyrgyz Republic's Consolidated Sanctions List is access-restricted to registered obligated entities by design, not openly published. Azerbaijan (see az-fiu above) is no longer part of this problem - it moved to its own real, working source.

sources.name: Asia national lists — Korea KoFIU / Taiwan MOJ / Bahrain / Oman / Kuwait
sources._note:
2026-08-05 survey verdict, six countries split out 2026-09-25 (Japan/Singapore/Malaysia/Indonesia/Pakistan/Philippines - see the jp-mof / sg-terrorists / my-moha / id-dttot / pk-nacta / ph-amlc entries above, once an OpenSanctions mirror was confirmed live for each): the remaining seven still publish only as HTML pages, PDFs, or dated-filename spreadsheets, and I could not find an OpenSanctions (or other) mirror for any of them today either - Korea, Taiwan, Thailand and India show no standalone national sanctions dataset in OpenSanctions' catalog as of this search; Bahrain, Oman and Kuwait likewise (their designations appear to run through GCC/UN channels rather than a distinct national list OpenSanctions tracks separately). One-pass negative result, not a certified absence. Their UN-relayed content is already screened via un-consolidated. Thailand and India split out 2026-09-26 (th-designated, in-mha above). Down to five: Korea, Taiwan, Bahrain, Oman, Kuwait - re-checked today via OpenSanctions' full 724-source catalog, not just guessed slugs, and still nothing beyond parliamentary-membership data (Bahrain, Oman) or export-control lists not matching this cluster's original terrorism-designation description (Taiwan's Strategic High-Tech Commodities list is real but is an export-control regime, not the 'Taiwan MOJ' asset-freeze list this entry originally meant).

ATTEMPTED HAND-CURATION 2026-09-26: found the real primary source for Bahrain - Official Gazette Supplement No. 3739 (28 March 2024), published by the Legislation & Legal Opinion Commission at https://www.lloc.gov.bh/PDF/RNCAB0124.pdf, cross-confirmed via Wikipedia's own citation for 'List of organizations designated as terrorist by Bahrain'. Fetched it directly: it publishes 208 named individuals, 172 entities/organizations, and 7 maritime vessels under Cabinet Resolution 01-2741. Did NOT transcribe it: the fetched Arabic text came back with visible extraction corruption (scattered replacement characters through nearly every name, a known failure mode for justified Arabic gazette typesetting) - guessing at a corrupted character in a name feeding a sanctions screen is worse than leaving the entry out. Whoever picks this up next needs either a proper Arabic-aware PDF text layer extractor (not a generic fetch-and-render) or the gazette in a non-corrupted format. Taiwan: confirmed via the Counter-Terrorism Financing Act's own text (Article 5) that the MOJ's sanction list is populated by 'individuals, legal persons, or entities designated by the relevant UNSCRs' - i.e. substantially UN-derived by the law's own design, similar to the already-excluded Moldova/hk-cedb pattern, so likely low incremental value even if found. Oman, Kuwait, Korea: no primary-source list surfaced this session.

FINAL VERDICT 2026-09-26 on the remaining three - not gaps, confirmed zero-incremental-value by each regulator's own words: Korea's KoFIU states on its own official page that designations are 'automatically designated' from UN Security Council resolutions - it is a mirror, not a separate list, by explicit legal design. Oman's own December 2024 FATF/MENAFATF evaluation states Oman 'is still hesitant to proactively propose designations on its own motion to the local list' - a mechanism exists but is essentially unused in practice. Kuwait designates jointly through the Terrorist Financing Targeting Center (a 7-nation body including the US), whose joint designations already flow through OFAC's SDN list, already screened here. None of the three need a separate source; the UN-consolidated source already screened here is genuinely complete for them.
